patch.value: GH-1706: a stale session-state lock makes pm release clear the claim and then exit 4, --force repeats the refusal, and claim only warns

GH-1706 (filed 2026-11-11). A stale session-state lock (expired TTL from a crashed agent) makes claim and release disagree, and release reports failure after it has written. On a fresh tracker: pm claim exits 0 with the claim_semantic_attribution_unrecorded warning and records the claim; pm release exits 4 with 'Item session-state lock is stale; rerun with --force when supported for this command' but the claim is already removed; pm release --force exits 4 with the same text; pm health reports stale_lock_count 1 with remedy pm gc --scope locks. Four problems: a partial write reported as a failure, two policies for one condition, a recovery hint naming a flag that cannot succeed, and wording that attributes the lock to an item. Expected: release refuses before any mutation or succeeds with the same attribution warning claim uses; one policy for a stale session-state lock across claim, start, release and close (reclaiming an expired TTL automatically is simplest); the refusal or warning names pm gc --scope locks and the lock path and never recommends an unusable flag. pm-rust mirrors the published behaviour (pm-rust#165).

release never mutates and then exits non-zero on a stale session-state lock; claim, start, release and close share one policy for a stale session-state lock; The refusal or warning names pm gc --scope locks and the lock path, never an unusable flag, and attributes the lock to session state
One consistent outcome for a stale session-state lock with a working recovery
release removes the claim then exits 4; --force repeats the refusal
